identity.title: Food Safety Plan – Ready-to-Eat Hummus and Bean Dips (Salem Plant)
identity.issuer: Willamette Valley Foods, Inc. (prepared by Dana Whitfield, Quality Manager/PCQI; approved by Plant Manager)

scan.summary: This is the company's own written Food Safety Plan under FDA's Preventive Controls for Human Food rule (21 CFR Part 117), covering hazard analysis, preventive controls, monitoring, corrective actions, verification, a supply-chain program, records and training for the Salem plant's refrigerated hummus and bean dip line. It shows real operating detail (cook, cooling, sanitation, allergen and metal-detection controls with critical limits) but is missing several elements the rule requires the plan to contain.
scan.freshness_note: The plan is dated effective May 12, 2025, so it is a little over a year old as of September 2026. 21 CFR 117.170(a) requires reanalysis of the plan as a whole at least once every 3 years, which would put the next required reanalysis by May 12, 2028 — but the plan itself does not state this schedule (see gap below), so there is no internal marker showing whether that review is already planned.

gaps.title: No written recall plan
gaps.description: The plan has no recall plan section. Section 8 (supply-chain) is followed directly by Section 9 (records) and Section 10 (training); nothing addresses notifying consignees, notifying the public when needed, checking recall effectiveness, or disposing of recalled product.
gaps.fix: Add a recall plan section describing procedures to notify direct consignees, notify the public when appropriate, conduct effectiveness checks, and appropriately dispose of recalled product.
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 117.139(a)-(b), required as a plan element by 21 CFR 117.126(b)(4)

gaps.title: Plan approval not shown as signed and dated
gaps.description: The cover page names an approver but shows no actual signature or date, so there is no evidence the owner, operator, or agent in charge signed and dated the plan as required.
gaps.fix: Obtain a physical or verifiable electronic signature and date from the Plant Manager (or owner/operator/agent in charge) on the plan, and re-sign upon any future modification.

gaps.title: No documented validation of preventive controls
gaps.description: Critical limits are stated (212°F/60 min cook, cooling curve, metal detector reject sizes) but there is no reference to scientific or technical evidence, or a study, showing these controls actually achieve control of the identified hazards. Section 7 covers verification (record review, calibration, product testing) but not validation.
gaps.fix: Obtain and document validation (published scientific/technical evidence, a challenge study, or expert determination) for each process preventive control, performed or overseen by the PCQI, and keep it as a record.

gaps.title: No stated reanalysis schedule
gaps.description: The plan does not state that it will be reanalyzed as a whole at least once every 3 years, nor list the other required triggers (significant facility change, new hazard information, an unanticipated food safety problem, or a control found ineffective).
gaps.fix: Add a statement that the PCQI will reanalyze the plan at least every 3 years from the effective date (next due by May 12, 2028) and upon any of the listed triggering events, with reanalysis records kept.

gaps.title: Supply-chain program lacks verification-activity detail
gaps.description: Section 8 says approved suppliers must provide a third-party audit certificate and a certificate of analysis, but does not show who approves suppliers and on what hazard basis, how the type and frequency of verification activity was determined, or whether an onsite audit is required for any hazard (e.g., the sesame allergen or a biological hazard in tahini/dry beans) controlled by the supplier.
gaps.fix: Document the hazard-based approval and verification-activity determination for each raw material, including whether onsite audits are required, the frequency of verification, and who (a qualified individual) makes and documents these determinations.
gaps.quote: Tahini and dry beans are received only from approved suppliers who provide a current third-party audit certificate and a certificate of analysis for each lot.

gaps.title: No training records named
gaps.description: Section 10 states employees receive food hygiene training at hire and annually, but unlike the cook, cooling, ATP, metal-detection, and label logs named elsewhere in the plan, no training log or record is identified to show who was trained, when, and on what topic.
gaps.fix: Name and maintain a training log (employee name, date, topic, trainer) and retain it under the plan's existing two-year record retention policy in Section 9.
gaps.quote: All production employees receive food hygiene training at hire and annually.

deadlines.title: Probe thermometer calibration
deadlines.source_line: Probe thermometers are calibrated in ice water and boiling water weekly

deadlines.title: Metal detector manufacturer service
deadlines.source_line: the metal detector is serviced by the manufacturer annually

deadlines.title: Finished product Listeria monocytogenes testing
deadlines.source_line: Finished product is tested for Listeria monocytogenes monthly by an accredited laboratory

deadlines.title: Environmental monitoring trend review
deadlines.source_line: Environmental monitoring results are trended quarterly

deadlines.title: Employee food hygiene training
deadlines.source_line: All production employees receive food hygiene training at hire and annually

deadlines.title: PCQI review of monitoring records
deadlines.source_line: The PCQI reviews the cook, cooling, sanitation, allergen and metal detection records within seven working days of their creation

deadlines.title: PCQI review of corrective actions
deadlines.source_line: All corrective actions are recorded on the corrective action log and reviewed by the PCQI within seven days

facts.quote: The Salem plant operates one shift, five days a week, with 28 production employees.
facts.affects: Scale of the facility and training/monitoring workload the plan must cover
Refrigerated shelf life drives the Listeria monocytogenes hazard significance and the need for validated cold-chain and testing controls

facts.quote: Products are labeled with the allergen statement "Contains: sesame" for all hummus items.
facts.affects: Confirms sesame as the major allergen requiring dedicated allergen preventive controls and label review

facts.quote: for retail sale in Oregon, Washington and Idaho
facts.affects: Multistate retail distribution; relevant to which state agencies beyond Oregon could have an interest in recalls
Establishes the PCQI's qualification date for oversight of validation, reanalysis, and record review duties

facts.value: At least two years from the date of the record
facts.quote: All records named in this plan are kept at the Salem plant for at least two years from the date of the record
facts.affects: Meets the general 2-year minimum retention baseline under Part 117 subpart F for the records named in the plan

expected_missing.title: Environmental monitoring program (written)
expected_missing.why: Companies running an EMP for Listeria in a refrigerated RTE plant typically keep a standalone written program describing site selection rationale, escalation, and trending beyond the brief mention here
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Supplier approval file / audit certificates and COAs on hand
expected_missing.why: Section 8 references audit certificates and certificates of analysis but the actual documents or an approved supplier list file usually sit alongside the plan
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Master sanitation schedule / SSOPs
expected_missing.why: A plant with this level of process detail usually has a separate sanitation standard operating procedure document supporting the ATP/Listeria swabbing described here
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Pest control program
expected_missing.why: Refrigerated RTE food plants typically document a pest control program as part of their prerequisite programs, not addressed in this plan
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Oregon food processing license/registration
expected_missing.why: A facility selling packaged retail food in Oregon typically holds a state food processor license from the Oregon Department of Agriculture, separate from this federal preventive-controls plan
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Employee training log
expected_missing.why: Named directly as a gap above, but companies at this scale typically already keep this as a matter of course alongside the other named logs
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

WILLAMETTE VALLEY FOODS, INC.
FOOD SAFETY PLAN
Ready-to-eat hummus and bean dips
Salem Plant, 1850 Fairgrounds Road NE, Salem, Oregon 97301
Effective date: May 12, 2025
Prepared by: Dana Whitfield, Quality Manager, Preventive Controls Qualified Individual
(PCQI certificate, FSPCA course, March 2024)
Approved by: Plant Manager
1. Facility and product description
Willamette Valley Foods produces refrigerated ready-to-eat hummus and bean dips in 8-ounce and 16-
ounce sealed plastic tubs for retail sale in Oregon, Washington and Idaho. The Salem plant operates one
shift, five days a week, with 28 production employees. Products are made from cooked chickpeas or black
beans, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, salt and spices, blended, filled, sealed, coded and held
refrigerated at or below 41°F. Shelf life is 45 days refrigerated. Products are labeled with the allergen
statement "Contains: sesame" for all hummus items.
2. Process flow
Receiving of dry beans, tahini and other ingredients → dry storage or refrigerated storage → soaking and
cooking of beans (kettle, 212°F, 60 minutes minimum) → cooling in the blast chiller → blending with
other ingredients → filling and sealing → date coding → metal detection → refrigerated storage →
shipping.
3. Hazard analysis

beans (Salmonella, Listeria monocytogenes) product

and Bacillus cereus spore-former outgrowth

storage shelf life

and ingredients
4. Preventive controls
Hazard Preventive control Type Critical limit or parameter
Vegetative Cook beans in the kettle to an internal temperature of at Process Minimum 212°F for 60 minutes, measured
pathogens at cook least 212°F for at least 60 minutes with a calibrated probe thermometer
Spore-former Cool cooked beans from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours Process 135°F to 70°F in 2 hours; 70°F to 41°F in
growth at cooling and to 41°F within a further 4 hours in the blast chiller 4 hours
Listeria in the Sanitation of food-contact surfaces before each Sanitation ATP swab pass before start-up; Listeria
RTE environment production run and between products; environmental spp. swabs, 10 sites weekly, zone 1 and 2
monitoring swabs weekly
Sesame allergen Allergen labeling review for every label at receipt and at Allergen Label matches the formulation sheet;
printing; product scheduling with hummus items last in washdown verified by ATP swab before
the day, followed by full washdown the next non-sesame product
Metal Metal detection of every sealed tub Process Reject at 2.0 mm ferrous, 2.5 mm non-
ferrous, 3.0 mm stainless test pieces
5. Monitoring
The kettle operator records the internal temperature and the time at the start and end of each cook batch
on the cook log. The blast chiller operator records the temperature at 2 hours and at 6 hours on the cooling
log. The sanitation lead records the ATP swab result before each start-up. The line lead runs the three
metal test pieces through the detector at start-up, every two hours, and at the end of the run, and records
the result. The quality technician reviews every label lot against the formulation sheet at receipt and signs
the label log.
6. Corrective actions
If a cook batch does not reach 212°F for 60 minutes, the batch is re-cooked to the critical limit or
discarded, and the cause is recorded. If cooling exceeds the time limits, the batch is discarded. If an ATP
swab fails, the surface is re-cleaned and re-swabbed before production starts. If a Listeria spp. swab is
positive, the site is cleaned and re-swabbed, adjacent sites are added, and product made on that line since
the last negative swab is held pending investigation. If the metal detector fails a test piece, all product
since the last passing test is re-run through the detector. If a label does not match the formulation, the lot
is quarantined and not used. All corrective actions are recorded on the corrective action log and reviewed
by the PCQI within seven days.
7. Verification
The PCQI reviews the cook, cooling, sanitation, allergen and metal detection records within seven
working days of their creation. Probe thermometers are calibrated in ice water and boiling water weekly,
and the metal detector is serviced by the manufacturer annually. Finished product is tested for Listeria
monocytogenes monthly by an accredited laboratory. Environmental monitoring results are trended
quarterly.
8. Supply-chain program
Tahini and dry beans are received only from approved suppliers who provide a current third-party audit
certificate and a certificate of analysis for each lot. The approved supplier list is maintained by the quality
manager.
9. Records
All records named in this plan are kept at the Salem plant for at least two years from the date of the record
and are available to FDA and the Oregon Department of Agriculture on request. Records are reviewed and
signed by the PCQI as described in section 7.
10. Training
All production employees receive food hygiene training at hire and annually. The PCQI holds a current
FSPCA certificate. Sanitation and line leads are trained on the monitoring procedures in this plan.
